items.prompt:
A word specific to a field (like 'inflation') is a:
A) technical term
B) rhyme
C) title

The feeling a word carries beyond its meaning is its:
A) connotation
B) spelling
C) syllables

Which has a more NEGATIVE connotation?
A) frugal
B) miserly
C) thrifty

Read.

Inflation, a rise in prices over time, erodes savings.

'Inflation' means:
A) falling prices
B) a rise in prices over time
C) a type of tax
items.answer: B) a rise in prices over time

steps: Defined in text. Key is B.
solution.answer: B) a rise in prices over time

items.prompt:
Read.

The policy was a Band-Aid, covering the problem without curing it.

The analogy means the policy was:
A) a permanent cure
B) only a temporary, surface fix
C) made of plastic
items.answer: B) only a temporary, surface fix

solution.answer: B) only a temporary, surface fix

items.prompt:
Calling a government program 'a Trojan horse for new taxes' is an allusion suggesting it:
A) hides a harmful purpose inside an appealing offer
B) is about ancient Greece
C) involves horses
items.answer: A) hides a harmful purpose inside an appealing offer

steps: Allusion = hidden threat. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) hides a harmful purpose inside an appealing offer

items.prompt:
One newspaper calls a budget cut 'tightening our belts'; another calls it 'gutting vital services.' This shows how word choice can:
A) shape readers' feelings about the same policy through connotation
B) only affect spelling
C) change nothing
items.answer: A) shape readers' feelings about the same policy through connotation

steps: Loaded words steer opinion. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) shape readers' feelings about the same policy through connotation

items.prompt:
Why do informational authors DEFINE technical terms?
A) so readers understand field-specific vocabulary precisely
B) to pad the text
C) to confuse readers
items.answer: A) so readers understand field-specific vocabulary precisely

solution.answer: A) so readers understand field-specific vocabulary precisely
